text:
maya: Running nightly long-seq stress on Dedicated pool and seeing intermittent NaNs in the attention path. Blamed kernel is `flashx-lite-fused-v2` when batching and KV cache are both active. Repro on 8xA100 under load.
jorge: Can you paste the minimal repro and the log snippet where the NaN shows up?

maya: Log excerpt:
```
2025-08-18 03:04:12.412 [worker-12] WARN runtime::attn: nan detected in softmax output (kernel=flashx-lite-fused-v2)
2025-08-18 03:04:12.413 [worker-12] ERROR runtime::request: failing request 0x7f3a... -> 500
```
Repro command (docker):
```
./runtest --model redwood-13b --kernel flashx-lite-fused-v2 --batching continuous --max-batch 128 --seq 2048 --kv-hot 1 --quant fp8 --rounding nearest_even --seed 42
```
This fails ~1/350 runs under concurrency 48, seq=2048.

sophie: I profiled the failing run. Flame shows a brief 12ms spike in the fused kernel right before the nan. nvprof snippet (relevant):
```
Device Kernel: flashx_fused_softmax_forward 12.1ms
Device Kernel: kv_store_prefetch 1.3ms
```
Throughput is fine otherwise -> looks numeric, not mem corruption.

li: Two quick hypotheses: (1) fp8 quant + fused kernel accumulates without proper fp32 accumulation and softmax exponent overflow occurs, (2) prefix/KV caching changes exponent distribution -> larger logits. Workarounds to try:
- clamp logits before exp: logits = min(logits, 60.0)
- add eps in softmax denom: denom = max(sum_exp, 1e-8)
- cast accumulator to bf16/fp32 before exp and reductions
Also try `ATTN_NUMERIC_GUARD=1` env var (dev flag) which forces per-block softmax fallback to bf16.

maya: Tried the env var locally -> crashes disappeared in 800+ runs. Good signal. But perf regression ~8-10% p99 latency.

kevin: Quick patch idea: in fused kernel, do softmax accumulation in bf16 (or fp32 if available) for the reduction path only; leave the majority of matmul in fp8 to keep perf. I opened PR #4567 with the change (adds bf16 accumulation path and a small clamp). Bench numbers attached to PR show p99 +2% vs baseline and no NaNs in 10k runs on CI.

jorge: Can we gate this behind a rollout flag? We should avoid global rollback if we can.

maya: Agreed. Suggest `flashx-lite-fp8-safety` feature flag that enables the accumulation fallback when we detect long-seq + large batch + kv-hot. We already detect those heuristics in the kernel selector.

infra-bot: deploy/canary flashx-lite-fp8-safety=on started on dedicated-us-west-2 at 2025-08-18T10:22:00Z :rocket:

li: Follow-ups: add unit test that simulates skewed logits (e.g., random in [0, 100]) and runs fused kernel with Kv-prefetch enabled; CI should run it under the quantized path. Also capture the distribution of logits in metrics (histogram) so we can alert when tail > 40.

sophie: One more observation: this primarily showed up when continuous batching grouped many short prompts into a very long effective sequence (we saw combined seq > 4k tokens). So batching heuristic change (limit continuous batch concat for kv-hot flows) could avoid hitting the numeric extreme without perf fallout.

kevin: I'll update the PR to include a small clamp + perf-opted bf16 reduction and add the feature-flag toggle. If tests are green we can canary the change and then remove the flag after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

maya: Plan for next 48h: 1) land PR #4567 behind flag, 2) add CI reproducer test and logits histogram metric, 3) tweak batching heuristic to cap concat length for KV hot paths, 4) watch p99 and NaN alerts.

jorge: :thumbsup: Please post the PR link and the canary dashboard snapshot when available.

kevin: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4567 (wip)

maya: Thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated if we see any regression or new patterns. :eyes:
